rows.name: CLIFF_BYSTANDERS
rows.values: Integer, parsed with `atoi`. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A value above the maximum is lowered to the maximum.
rows.default: Unset: the test case uses the maximum. Empty: counts as `0`, and the test case skips.
rows.effect: Sets the largest number of bystander threads (extra waiting threads) that the test case `spin waiter storm at scale (56c cliff)` starts. Smaller rounds with 4, 8, 16 and 32 threads still run when they are not above this number. A result below 8 threads makes the test case skip.
rows.notes: The maximum is the number of application CPUs (CPU cores that the process pins its application threads to) minus 3, and at most 53 threads. `0` and negative values cause the skip. The skip message is `Not enough app cpus for a waiter storm`.

rows.name: CMAKE_ARGV
rows.values: Path of a file that the fake `cmake` writes.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `cmake` stops with an unbound variable error.
rows.effect: The fake `cmake` writes its arguments, each ended by a NUL byte, to this file.
rows.notes: The test runs `make` with the fake `cmake` first on `PATH`. It then reads the file and checks the `-DTRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE` argument.

rows.name: COLLISION_STATE
rows.values: Path of a state file.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `mv` stops with a bash parameter error.
rows.effect: While this file is missing, the fake `mv` first creates the destination directory and writes its path here.
rows.notes: The fake `mv` also writes an `owner` file into that directory. It then runs the real `mv` named by `REAL_MV`. The test runs `bin/ci/ci-shared-nfs.sh purge-entry` with it. `bin/ci/run-ci-helper-suites.sh` lists this test file as skipped.

rows.name: FAKE_MKDIR_RACE
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The test sets `1`.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `mkdir` creates the directory once.

rows.name: FAKE_MKDIR_READONLY
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The test sets `1`.

rows.notes: The fake `mkdir` acts only on a directory directly under `$FAKE_TRACEFS/instances`. The test calls `prepare_tracefs` of `perfetto/launcher-common`.

rows.default: Unset: the fake `mkdir` sends no signal.

rows.name: FAKE_NIX_OUTPUT

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT
rows.values: Integer exit status, passed to `exit`. An empty text counts as unset. The test sets `0`, `23` and an empty text.
rows.default: Unset: after its readiness step, the fake `perfetto` runs until it gets `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`.
rows.effect: After its readiness step, the fake `perfetto` waits and then exits with this status.
rows.notes: The readiness step writes one byte to the descriptor given by `--notify-fd`. Before the exit the program waits for the file named by `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_MARKER`, or it sleeps `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_DELAY` seconds. `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_BEFORE_NOTIFY`, or `FAKE_PERFETTO_NOTIFY_STATUS` other than `0`, makes it exit earlier with this status.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_BEFORE_NOTIFY
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The test sets `1`.
rows.default: Unset: the fake `perfetto` does not exit at this point.
rows.effect: The fake `perfetto` exits before it writes the ready byte to the `--notify-fd` descriptor.
rows.notes: The exit status is the value of `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT`. The status is `0` when that variable is unset or empty.

rows.name: FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_DELAY
rows.values: Number of seconds, passed unchanged to `sleep`. The test sets `0.05` and `0.2`.
rows.default: Unset: 0 seconds.
rows.effect: The fake `perfetto` sleeps this many seconds before it exits with the status of `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT`.
rows.notes: It has an effect only when `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT` is not empty and `FAKE_PERFETTO_EXIT_MARKER` is unset or empty.

new_terms.definition: A CPU core in the list that a TRON process pins its application threads to.
An extra waiting thread that the test `t_mwaitx_cliff` starts next to the 2 threads that it measures.

notes: All 24 rows are kept. 23 rows are fixtures (hand_set false). Only CLIFF_BYSTANDERS is set by a person. No row is dropped. 4 evidence quotes are an exact part of the source line and not the whole line: perfetto/test_perfetto.py:121, :124 and :125 (2 quotes). The rest of each line holds the shell operator made of 2 vertical bar characters, which the table format forbids. The `default` cells of EXAMPLE_MOUNT, EXAMPLE_MOUNT_STATUS, EXAMPLE_UNMOUNT and FAKE_NIX_OUTPUT stay empty. The test sets these 4 variables before every run of the fake program. The second sentence of the CLIFF_BYSTANDERS effect cell rests on t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:221, which is not among the 4 evidence lines.

changes.name: CLIFF_BYSTANDERS
changes.was: Unset: the test uses the maximum.
changes.now: Unset: the test case uses the maximum. Empty: counts as `0`, and the test case skips.
changes.why: An empty value differs from unset. `std::atoi` of an empty text returns 0 (t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:202). A count below 8 skips the test case (t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:208). Unset keeps `n_bystanders = max_bystanders` (t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:199).

changes.name: CLIFF_BYSTANDERS

changes.now: Sets the largest number of bystander threads (extra waiting threads) that the test case `spin waiter storm at scale (56c cliff)` starts. Smaller rounds with 4, 8, 16 and 32 threads still run when they are not above this number. A result below 8 threads makes the test case skip.
changes.why: The value is the last step of a sweep, not the only thread count. The loop `for (int n : {4, 8, 16, 32, n_bystanders})` skips a step only when `n > n_bystanders` (t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:221, t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:222). The skip message moved to the notes cell.

changes.why: Wording only. The skip message comes from t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:209. The maximum comes from t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:197 and t/t_mwaitx_cliff.cpp:198.
